facts.fact_text: The first applicant participated in a demonstration organised by the opposition on 20 October 2012.
The second applicant participated in a demonstration organised by the opposition on 20 October 2012.
The second applicant participated in a demonstration held on 12 January 2013.
The second applicant participated in a demonstration held on 26 January 2013.
The third applicant participated in a demonstration held on 30 April 2013.
According to the applicants, the demonstrations were intended to be peaceful and were conducted in a peaceful manner.
The participants of the demonstration of 20 October 2012 were demanding democratic reforms in Azerbaijan and free and fair elections.
The participants of the demonstration of 20 October 2012 were protesting against impediments on freedom of assembly.
The demonstration of 12 January 2013 was aimed at protesting about the deaths of soldiers in the army.
The demonstration of 26 January 2013 condemned the use of force by the police against the participants of previous demonstrations.
The participants of the demonstration of 30 April 2013 were commemorating the victims of a terrorist attack committed in 2009 at the Azerbaijan State Oil Academy.
The police began to disperse the demonstration of 20 October 2012 as soon as the protesters began to gather.
The police began to disperse the demonstration of 12 January 2013 as soon as the protesters began to gather.
The police began to disperse the demonstration of 26 January 2013 as soon as the protesters began to gather.
The police began to disperse the demonstration of 30 April 2013 as soon as the protesters began to gather.

The circumstances related to the dispersal of the demonstration of 20 October 2012, the first and second applicants' arrests and custody, and subsequent administrative proceedings against them are similar to those in Gafgaz Mammadov v. Azerbaijan (no. 60259/11, judgment of 15 October 2015).

The circumstances related to the dispersal of the demonstrations of 12 January 2013, 26 January 2013, and 30 April 2013, the second and third applicants' arrests and custody, and the subsequent administrative proceedings against them are similar to those in Bayramov v. Azerbaijan ([Committee] nos. 19150/13 and 52022/13, judgment of 6 April 2017).
Law no. 135-IVQD of 31 May 2011 introduced amendments to the Code of Administrative Offences 2000 (the CAO), which entered into force on 1 July 2011.

After the amendments introduced by Law no. 135-IVQD of 31 May 2011, Article 410.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences 2000 provided that a copy of the administrative offence report shall be given to an individual who is subject to the administrative offence proceedings or to a representative of a legal entity.

After the amendments introduced by Law no. 135-IVQD of 31 May 2011, Article 410.4 of the Code of Administrative Offences 2000 provided that an aggrieved person in administrative offence proceedings has the right to a copy of the administrative offence report.

A summary of other relevant provisions concerning administrative proceedings, relevant provisions concerning freedom of assembly, the organisation and holding of public assemblies, and relevant extracts from international documents and press releases can be found in the judgment of Gafgaz Mammadov v. Azerbaijan (no. 60259/11, 15 October 2015) at paragraphs 27–30, 33–35, and 37–42.

A summary of other relevant provisions concerning administrative proceedings, relevant provisions concerning freedom of assembly, the organisation and holding of public assemblies, and relevant extracts from international documents and press releases can be found in the judgment of Abbasli v. Azerbaijan ([Committee] nos. 5417/13 and 73309/14, 16 February 2017) at paragraphs 23–25 and 28–29.
On 15 October 2012, prior to the demonstration of 20 October 2012, the organisers gave notice to the Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA).
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) refused to authorise the holding of the demonstration at the place indicated by the organisers.

The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) proposed a different location on the outskirts of Baku — the grounds of a driving school situated in the 20th residential area of the Sabail District — as an alternative venue for the demonstration.
Despite the Baku City Executive Authority's refusal to authorise the original location, the organisers decided to hold the demonstration as originally planned.
The organisers of the demonstrations held on 12 January 2013, 26 January 2013, and 30 April 2013 gave no proper prior notice to the Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA).
Information about the demonstrations held on 12 January 2013, 26 January 2013, and 30 April 2013 was disseminated on the internet or in the press.
The police began to disperse the demonstration of 20 October 2012 as soon as the protesters began to gather.
The police began to disperse the demonstration of 12 January 2013 as soon as the protesters began to gather.
The police began to disperse the demonstration of 26 January 2013 as soon as the protesters began to gather.
The police began to disperse the demonstration of 30 April 2013 as soon as the protesters began to gather.

The circumstances related to the dispersal of the demonstration of 20 October 2012, the first and second applicants' arrests and custody, and subsequent administrative proceedings against them are similar to those in Gafgaz Mammadov v. Azerbaijan (no. 60259/11, judgment of 15 October 2015).

The circumstances related to the dispersal of the demonstrations of 12 January 2013, 26 January 2013, and 30 April 2013, the second and third applicants' arrests and custody, and the subsequent administrative proceedings against them are similar to those in Bayramov v. Azerbaijan ([Committee] nos. 19150/13 and 52022/13, judgment of 6 April 2017).
